This is coming few months after the NDLEA dismantled a transnational Nigerian-Mexican methamphetamine syndicate, arresting a suspected drug baron, three Mexican nationals, and six other collaborators during coordinated operations in Ogun and Lagos States.
This new operation, which covered Lagos and Kano, prevented the cartel from moving 13.795 kilogrammes of cocaine through a carefully planned route involving air travel, road transportation and desert crossings through Niger Republic and Libya.
In a development that exposed the dangerous methods employed by drug trafficking networks, all eight suspects had swallowed cocaine pellets and were forced to remain in custody for medical observation until they excreted a combined 634 wraps of the illicit substance.
The arrests were made between October 30 and 31, 2026, following intelligence gathering and coordinated operations involving the NDLEA’s Special Operations Unit and Kano Command.
The operation began in Lagos with the arrest of a 57-year-old suspect, Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota. He subsequently excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650kg.
A day later, four other suspected members of the network were intercepted at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, while preparing to board a flight to Kano.
They were identified as Jackson Ahamefule, 43; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47; Marcel Nnabuike, 38; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44.
The four suspects later excreted 90, 85, 75 and 75 wraps of cocaine respectively, bringing the total recovered from the five suspects arrested in Lagos to 399 wraps weighing 8.655kg.
Intelligence gathered during the operation revealed that other members of the syndicate had already travelled to Kano, prompting the immediate mobilisation of NDLEA operatives at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport.
Three other suspects, Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31, were subsequently arrested at the arrival hall of the domestic terminal.
A body scan confirmed that the three men had also swallowed cocaine pellets. They were placed under observation and subsequently excreted 85, 80 and 70 pellets respectively, weighing a combined 5.140kg.
Investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly planned to move the drugs from Kano by road through Niger Republic and Libya before eventually transporting them to Europe.
The arrests have exposed the growing sophistication of international drug trafficking networks and the lengths to which their operators are willing to go to evade security agencies.
Reacting to the breakthrough, NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Marwa (retd.), commended officers of the Special Operations Unit and Kano Command for their intelligence-driven collaboration, describing the operation as a demonstration of the agency’s determination to close trafficking routes across the country.
Marwa said the cartel had attempted to exploit Nigeria’s northern borders and the Sahara Desert as an alternative route to Europe but was unsuccessful.
“This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara. Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria.
“Whether they go by air, by road or through the desert, we will trace them, find them and bring them to justice,” he said.
He also warned young Nigerians against allowing themselves to be recruited as drug couriers, particularly through the dangerous practice of swallowing cocaine pellets.
According to him, the rupture of even one pellet inside the body could cause death, stressing that no financial reward was worth risking one’s life for drug traffickers.
“Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish. One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk,” Marwa warned.
